descriptor.scene: Chrissy is the subject, caught in the exact second of the find: she stands at the right of frame with one arm still holding back a heavy curtain of vines, and behind the parted green the portal stands found and open exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light, thin brighter rim, small gold motes, lower tip floating above the ferns, warm gold spilling onto the mossy floor. Through the opening: warm light and a hint of sky only. On its short braided cream cord around her neck, the orange compass rests at her collarbone, its dark needle pointing straight at the light. But Chrissy's body is already turning back toward camera-left, one foot pivoted, face lit half by portal-gold and half by trail-green, mouth opening into the grin of someone about to run and tell. The portal occupies the right third; her turning figure carries the middle-left; the lower left corner stays calm trail. Caption pos is top, so the upper band stays simple canopy shadow.
descriptor._caption: It is Chrissy who finds it, on an ordinary morning, where the needle pointed, behind a curtain of vines she almost did not pull back. She does not climb a rock. She does not gather a crowd. She turns around and goes to get her friends.
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
the floating island visible through the opening (warm light and a hint of sky only here)
an antique compass-rose, star, points, tick marks, letters or numbers on the compass face (the face is plain warm cream with ONE dark clay-tipped needle only)

CHRISSY: a white woman with long wavy blonde hair worn down, center-parted, past the shoulders, a warm wide-open bright smile, in a relaxed cream or white blazer over a simple top. Quick, generous, lit up by having something to share. Warm-editorial ink-and-wash, never photoreal. Identity of record; wardrobe and features exactly as the locked sheets. the-portal exactly as its reference plate: A doorway of pure warm light hidden in the jungle: one upright pointed-oval of warm golden light, soft-edged like wet ink-wash with a thin brighter rim, its lower tip floating a hand's width above the forest floor. No frame, no ring, no arch, no standing stones, no machinery, no doorsill: the light alone is the door. Each era gets exactly one portal, and it shrinks: the more founders pass through and the longer it stands open, the smaller it gets, until it closes and leaves a flat ring of pale gold blossoms on the forest floor. Every portal in every era is this same design at some size. This era's portal at its opening is 3.8 m tall by 2.0 m wide: about twice a person's height, so a founder walks in without ducking and an adult's head reaches only halfway up the opening. Waning, the same shape shrinks to about 1.0 m, knee-to-waist high on an adult. Closed, a flat blossom ring about 2.0 m across lies on the forest floor. The lower tip always floats a hand's width (0.15 m) above the floor. The portal stands still; it never drifts, tilts or hovers higher. State-dependent only. Hidden: hanging vines, broad leaves and leaf-shadow curtain the light so only warm slivers show through; a passerby would walk within arm's length and never know. Master (found): the vines drawn aside, the oval open and generous, warm gold light with a few small drifting motes, soft warm glow on the nearest leaves. Waning: the same portal small and low, light gentler, the green closing in around it. Closed: no light at all, a quiet flat ring of pale gold blossoms in the green, moss and ferns grown back inside it. Nothing is ever scorched, broken or ominous. At its opening, about twice a person's height and wider than a garden gate; a closed ring reads about as wide as a person is tall lying down. In a wide shot the live portal is a tall warm almond of light against the green, unmistakably person-scaled, never building-scaled and never coin-scaled. An unbranded object inside the fable: never a company name, never a logo, never lettering on the face, the crate or the parachute. The shell's orange is the universe's existing clay/orange family (the same family as Maya's rust scarf), matte and warm, never neon and never safety-vest orange. Small in frame almost everywhere: a palm-sized object held, hung from a pack strap, or resting on a map. 'Smart' is shown only by the needle: it always swings toward the live portal, decisively, and may glow very faintly warm in dim scenes, never like a screen. No buttons, dials, antennas or lights are ever added. THE ONLY CHARACTERS IN THIS IMAGE ARE: chrissy. NOBODY ELSE APPEARS. Do not add any other person, figure, creature, robot, animal or bystander, whatever the style description above may suggest. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image, the floating island visible through the opening (warm light and a hint of sky only here), an antique compass-rose, star, points, tick marks, letters or numbers on the compass face (the face is plain warm cream with ONE dark clay-tipped needle only). ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
